details:
This is a potential solution for object/shader based crashers. I'm not an expert in cybersecurity so I don't know the resource demand on this or whether it's possible, so I'm only suggesting it as a concept.
Sandboxing in this context would be to test the upload in an isolated simulated environment that would mimic the end-user environment. In this case, it's mostly just Unity. This test would force enable everything on the avatar at once, and if it crashes, then it fails the test and rejects the upload. This may be applied to both Avatars and Worlds.
It would be unrealistic to expect this test to run through all existing avatars, so it may be something that would bear fruit in the long run where existing crashers would progressively get removed and new crashers rarely or no longer are made.
Furthermore, if this is a high demanding simulation, it may be worth at least simulating it in the user's own environment pre-upload. While it may get circumvented by malicious users or those willing to cluelessly sacrifice their security for a script kiddy SDK, it's better than no measures at all.
More technical details: To avoid a probably naïve approach such as "Enable Everything". The test could first run through a simple "Limiter" test to make sure than nothing on the avatar exceeds its safe count. Ignore Meshes as long as they're not stupidly high like 1 million tris. Run materials on simple meshes like a sphere, and so on. This definitely gets more complicated when getting into animations but it's a progressive security build.
title: Sandboxing Uploads
